questions.text: Why does the lesson describe prompt engineering as a pedagogical skill rather than a technical one?

options.text: Because it rests on the clear, structured communication teachers already use when writing assignment briefs, objectives and evaluation criteria.
Because it requires a background in programming that teachers acquire during initial teacher education.
Because the AI tools in question were designed specifically for schools.
Because it can only be learned through trial and error with a class present.

questions.explanation: The lesson argues that writing a good prompt is very close to writing a clear assignment brief — the underlying skill of purposeful, structured communication is identical, and only the audience changes from a class to a language model.

questions.text: Having to refine an AI response through follow-up instructions is a sign that the original prompt was badly written.
questions.explanation: The lesson presents iteration as the normal way the process works: the first prompt sets the direction and follow-up prompts refine the result. It states explicitly that needing to revise is not a sign that the original prompt was bad.

questions.text: Which statements about the prompting techniques covered in this lesson are accurate?

options.text: Assigning a role, such as "You are a Year 7 biology teacher", conveys audience, vocabulary level, tone and pedagogical approach in a few words.
Few-shot prompting means supplying one or more examples of the output you want so the AI can use them as a template.
Chain-of-thought prompting means asking the AI to work through its reasoning step by step, which also makes its work easier to check.
Constraining the scope means keeping the prompt itself as short as possible.
Providing examples is a technique that only works for mathematics tasks.

questions.explanation: Role assignment is presented as an efficient way to package several layers of context at once, few-shot prompting as showing rather than describing the output you want, and chain-of-thought prompting as making the reasoning transparent enough to verify. Constraining the scope concerns limits on the output — length, number of items, difficulty, topic — not the length of the prompt.

questions.text: What is the main practical benefit of stating your expectations and criteria — format, structure, required elements — in the original prompt?

options.text: It removes the need for avoidable follow-up requests, such as asking afterwards for an answer key or a name field.
It makes the AI generate its response noticeably faster.
It guarantees that the content the AI produces is factually accurate.
It lets the AI apply the same preferences automatically in your future conversations.

questions.explanation: The lesson's worksheet example shows that describing precisely what a good result looks like eliminates the round of "Can you add an answer key?" requests — the more precisely you state expectations, the less revision is needed afterwards.
